29 Two large parallel plates X and Y are placed a distance of 5.0 mm apart and connected to the
terminals of a 200 V d.c. supply, as shown.
X
Y
P
5.0 mm
200 V
A small oil drop at P carries one excess electron.
What is the magnitude of the electrostatic force acting on the oil drop due to the electric field
between the plates?
A
6.4 × 10–15 N
B
6.4 × 10–18 N
C
1.6 × 10–19 N
D
4.0 × 10–24 N

hints: Notice the plates form a uniform field with $V = 200 \text{ V}$ across separation $5.0 \text{ mm}$ at point P.
Recall the uniform-field relation $E = V/d$ for the parallel plates and $F = qE$ for a charge in that field.
Convert $5.0 \text{ mm}$ to metres and use $q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ for one excess electron, then multiply to find $F$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: potential difference $V = 200 \text{ V}$, plate separation $d = 5.0 \text{ mm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, and charge $q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ for one electron.
State the rule for a uniform field between large parallel plates: electric field strength $E = V/d$ is constant at P.
Substitute values with units: $E = 200 / (5.0 \times 10^{-3}) = 4.0 \times 10^4 \text{ V m}^{-1}$.
State the force rule on a charge in an electric field: $F = qE$.
Substitute: $F = (1.60 \times 10^{-19}) \times (4.0 \times 10^4) = 6.4 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$, with unit newton checked from $\text{C} \times \text{V m}^{-1}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Field $E = V/d = 4.0 \times 10^4 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ gives $F = qE = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \times 4.0 \times 10^4 = 6.4 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$.

B.explanation: This uses $d = 5.0 \text{ m}$ instead of $5.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, giving a field 1000 times too small.

C.explanation: This is just the charge of one electron and omits multiplication by the electric field strength $E = V/d$.

D.explanation: This value is far too small and does not follow from $E = V/d$ combined with $F = qE$ using $q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
